SGP Results for 2025

RICAS SGP Analyses in 2025: RICAS
• Two types of SGP analyses were conducted for 2025 RICAS data:
• Cohort referenced analyses: These analyses create growth norms from the
2023, 2024 and 2025 students. These growth norms yield cohort mean
(rounded)/median SGPs of 50.
• Baseline referenced analyses: Historical growth norms were created using
from 2017, 2018 and 2019 data. These growth norms (actually, coefficient
matrices) are applied to 2023, 2024, and 2025 data. These growth growth
analyses don’t have mean/median SGPs of 50 and can be used to investigate
overall COVID-19 academic recovery as well as potential scale drift
• Projections (lagged and straight) were calculated for 2025 data using
both cohort and baseline growth norms.

RICAS SGP Analyses in 2025: PSAT/SAT
• Two types of SGP analyses were conducted for PSAT to SAT data 2025
(single prior SAT growth data):
• Cohort referenced analyses: These analyses create growth norms from the 2024
and 2025 students. These growth norms yield cohort means/median SGPs of 50.
• Baseline referenced analyses: Historical growth norms were created using from
2018 and 2019 data. These growth norms (actually, coefficient matrices) are
applied to 2024, and 2025 data. These growth growth analyses don’t have
mean/median SGPs of 50 and can be used to investigate overall COVID-19
academic recovery (NOTE: In the base year, mean/median of SGPs is 50)
• No projections were calculated as the SAT (grade 11) is the last grade
tested in Rhode Island.

2025 SGP Results
• The cohort referenced results, not surprisingly, all center on 50. Goodness
of fit plots all show excellent model fit (uniform distribution of percentiles
across all levels of initial achievement)
• The baseline referenced results (referenced to pre-pandemic growth
norms/rates of learning) show:
• ELA mostly near 50 with two exceptions: Grade 4 with a mean of 47.8
and Grade 7 with a mean of 54.5.
• Mathematics Grades 5, 6, and 7 are well below 50 with Grade 4 above
50 and grades 8 and 11 near 50.
• In the following section we dig deeper into results with regard to growth
changes over time.

Examining growth trends over time
• Taking account of what grades the students were in when the
pandemic happened, we can examine both how this cohort grew
over time as well as how the system “adapted” as they increased
from grade to grade.
• For example, one caution expressed following the pandemic was
that students whose early literacy instruction was severely
disrupted could face increased risk of downstream academic
adversity due to inadequate foundational skills.
• We consider, for example, the students currently in Grade 7 who
were in Grade 2 (spring 2020) and Grade 3 (2020-2021 academic
year).

Pandemic Related Academic Recovery in Rhode Island 11

Examining growth trends over time
• We can also examine growth trends for the same grade over time.
• Larger changes in growth for the same grade over a 1 year time
span would be indicative of scale drift.
• Smaller changes could represent changes in educational efficacy or
(as we just investigated) different cohorts of students passing
through the grade with differing educational needs due to
pandemic related educational disruptions earlier in the students
schooling.

Summary
• Cohort-referenced SGPs showed excellent fit and as such are suitable for use as
part of accountability system calculations.
• Baseline-referenced SGPs showed un-even results with some grade/content area
pairs showing rates of learning above pre-pandemic levels and others showing
rates of learning below pre-pandemic levels.
• Extending these comparisons to prior years shows uneven types of changes
undermining several education related mechanisms that could potentially explain
the observed changes.
• Continued problems with Equating/linking results over time can not be ruled out
at this time as a potential explanation.
